Content: Just a bit of information that was left out. Bill Clinton got rid of legislation that was written during the Great Depression called the Glass-Steghall Act of 1933. This legislation was created to protect people from banks using the money in people's bank accounts to gamble with on the stock market. Though it isn't entirely the reason that the housing crisis happened, getting rid of the Glass-Stegahll Act of 1933 set the stage to make these predatory loans legal. More technically, it separated commercial banking and investment banking. This was something Republican lawmakers had dreamed of doing since it was first enacted by FDR but Bill Clinton got to it first.
